Why this matters

Two things push young Zimbabweans out of the classroom and out of work: unpaid fees, and a labour market with too few entry points. We work on both.

1 in 3

children in our partner communities have missed a term of school over unpaid fees.

41%

youth unemployment nationally, the reason our training tracks end in a trade, not a certificate alone.

US$45

covers one child's term fees, levies and stationery at a partner government school.

School fees project

Sponsor a learner's term

Every term, we sit with head teachers across three districts to see whose fees are owed. A missed payment means a child is sent home, sometimes for good. Your donation is paid directly to the school, against an invoice, before the term starts.

Where a $45 donation goes

We keep this simple and auditable: money goes to the school bursar, not to families directly, and every sponsor receives a receipt with the learner's school and term.

Tuition & levies$28
Exercise books & stationery$9
Uniform contribution (once/year)$6
MYC administration$2

Currently supporting learners at 11 partner schools across Harare, Chitungwiza and Mutare.

Vocational training

Skills that turn into income

For learners who've finished school and young adults who left early, we run six-month, hands-on tracks with local artisans and small-business owners as instructors, built to end in a tool kit, a portfolio, and a first client, not just a certificate.

+
01

Tailoring & Fashion Design

6 months · Harare studio

Pattern-cutting, machine work and finishing, ending with a small collection learners can sell. Past graduates now run stalls at Mbare and Avondale markets.

+
02

Carpentry & Joinery

6 months · Workshop-based

Furniture-making and basic building carpentry, with a local contractor hosting a two-month site placement in the final stretch.

+
03

Welding & Fabrication

5 months · Workshop-based

Gate, window-frame and furniture fabrication, high-demand skills in every growing township, taught with borrowed equipment from a partner garage.

+
04

Hair & Beauty Therapy

4 months · Salon placement

Braiding, cutting and skincare basics, with the final month spent working paid shifts inside a partner salon.

+
05

Agriculture & Agribusiness

6 months · Peri-urban plot

Market gardening, poultry and basic bookkeeping, for learners planning to farm family land or lease a plot on the edge of the city.

+
06

ICT & Digital Skills

4 months · Computer lab

Office software, mobile money systems and basic graphic design, aimed at admin, data-entry and freelance digital work.

Every track ends the same way: a graduation showcase where local employers and customers meet the cohort, plus a small starter kit of tools so the first job isn't blocked by equipment they can't yet afford.

Hire & teach

Bring your classroom or your workforce

Our vocational tracks run on contract instructors, and our graduates are looking for their first real job. Two ways to plug in directly.

Contract instructors

Teach a vocational track

We contract qualified tradespeople and teachers per cohort, typically 4 to 6 months, paid per module, with tools and workshop space provided at our partner sites.

Prefer email? Write to teach@maestroyouthcollective.org

Employer recruitment

Hire from our graduating cohort

Each graduation, roughly 30-40 trained young people are job-ready across six trades. Tell us what you need and we'll shortlist candidates from the matching track.

Prefer email? Write to hire@maestroyouthcollective.org
